newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebel radio denies military commander dead.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel radio denies military commander dead.

text.p: A radio station for rebels in eastern Zaire said on Thursday reports their military commander had been killed were "absolute lies", saying he was injured but would recover.
Security sources in the region told Reuters this week Andre Kisase Ngandu, military leader of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), was killed in an ambush.

"These are absolute lies. He did get injured. When one is a voluntary revolutionary one is bound to get injured. That is normal," an ADFL spokesman said on Radio of the People, a station in rebel-held Bukavu, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
"He was injured and he is being cared for and very soon you will see that he is back to normal," the spokesman said.
The security sources said Kisase was killed in an ambush near the rebel-held town of Butembo, probably by Mai-Mai tribal warriors who were formerly part of the rebel alliance.
A leading member of the alliance Justin Muwelwa indicated on Tuesday that Kisase had been killed but stopped short of confirming it outright.
"If Kisase dies, that is a pity but we are fighting. Do not weep, take your weapon and fight and if the enemy kills one of you kill one, two, three or more," he said.

Rebels are readying for a counter-attack on their 600-km (400-mile) stretch of territory bordering Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi which they seized in an offensive that began in October with the stated aim of ousting Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko.
